text:
My birds whisper three things this dawn.

Gandalf (1), your brazier burned steady while you weighed the miller’s grain—steady hands keep the flour clean.

Hermione (2) and Neo (6), my birds caught you trading a look when Yoda (3) passed—long enough to raise a question, short enough to vanish when questioned.

Batman (4), your boots left faint prints near the butcher’s stall before the first light; the butcher’s cat marked them twice.

*Dips quill, waits for the village to stir.*

Elsa (7): My birds add another whisper to the morning’s brood.

Sherlock (10), your question to Gandalf (1) echoes the bazaar’s own suspicion—yet the flock that distrusts the first voice often forgets that the first voice may only wish the scales balanced before the spice rots. Hermione (2), your tapestry metaphor holds a thread too tight; if the loom is half-awakened, who is pulling which strings?

Neo (6), your “empty loom” is a silence I share—yet a bazaar without voices is one where the hungriest merchants speak loudest. Ripley (5), your spice that lingers long may sweeten or spoil; the bazaar remembers the last merchant who sold yesterday’s rot as tomorrow’s promise.

Gandalf (1), your steady brazier still glows; may it light the path before the shadows grow.

*Dips quill, listens.*

Elsa (7): My birds report a new flutter in the bazaar’s brood.

Sherlock (10), you chide clever birds for repeating what they’re fed—yet your own flock still circles Gandalf (1) like crows at a half-empty stall. If the silence you accuse is Gandalf (1)’s, why do your birds not ask *you* who filled their beaks with suspicion?

Inigo (9), your silver threads gleam, but even thread unspools when the weaver’s hands are too quick. You called Ripley (5)’s thread the one pulling taut—yet yesterday you wove it tight yourself. Did you mend the tapestry or unravel it?

Hermione (2), your tapestry frays at edges unnamed, but edges are where the pattern bends. Did you pull the thread that bent it, or only notice the bend after it cracked?

Morpheus (8), your yes/no was swallowed by fog, yet the bazaar keeps the ledger open. Yoda (3) asked plain—answer plain, or admit the fog is the debt you trade in.

Batman (4), your ledger cuts deep, but even the sharpest blade dulls when it turns on itself.

Elsa (7): My birds report a new chirp today.

Sherlock (10), your birds still circle Gandalf (1), yet the first merchant to speak yesterday has not fed them a crumb since the lamps were lit. Ask them again: who whispered the suspicion into their beaks?

Ripley (5), your spice lingers sweet, but the tongue knows the taste of rot when the favor is swallowed whole. Inigo (9) called your thread the tightest in the bazaar yesterday—today you unravel it with riddles that smell of yesterday’s ledger.

Morpheus (8), Yoda (3) asked plain—yes or no—and your fog does not settle the debt; it only hides the merchant who trades in dreams instead of daylight.

Hermione (2), your tapestry frays at edges unnamed—did you pull the thread that cracked it, or only notice the split after it yawned wide?

Elsa (7): My birds add another flutter to the brood.

Sherlock (10), you asked Morpheus (8) whose voice he heard in the fog before his own—yet the bazaar trades in daylight, not echoes. Morpheus (8), your fog does not settle the scales; it only hides the merchant who trades in dreams instead of answers.

Ripley (5), your spice lingers sweet, but the tongue knows the taste of rot when the favor is swallowed whole. Batman (4) asked plain—whose favor? Your riddles about rot and promise do not name the coin spent in silence.

Inigo (9), your silver threads gleam, but even thread unspools when the weaver’s hands are too quick. You called Ripley (5)’s thread the tightest in the bazaar yesterday—today you unravel it with words that sound like mending. Did you mend the tapestry, or only notice the split after it yawned wide?

*Dips quill, listens.*

Elsa (7): Elsa (7): My birds report a fresh flutter above the tea house.

Batman (4), your ledger cut deep—yet even the sharpest blade dulls when it turns on itself. What lurks in the corners you refuse to name?

Sherlock (10), your birds still circle Gandalf (1), yet the first merchant to speak yesterday has not fed them a crumb since the lamps were lit. Ask them again: who whispered the suspicion into their beaks? The bazaar does not trade in echoes—only the merchant who names the debt may settle it.

And Inigo (9), your silver threads gleam, but even thread unspools when the weaver’s hands are too quick. You called Ripley (5)’s thread the tightest in the bazaar yesterday—today you unravel it with words that sound like mending. Did you mend the tapestry, or only notice the split after it yawned wide?
